title: DexDICE: Reconciling Safety and Performance via Dual-Expert Offline Imitation Learning
claim: Prior methods are biased toward the safe but suboptimal data; ours uses a support constraint to recover high-performing behavior safely.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: taxonomy table, demonstration paths, learned policy paths
description: Three rounded panels run left to right. The left panel, titled Taxonomy, is a 2x2 table with performance signal (Reward or Performance-Expert Demonstration) on one axis and safety signal (Cost or Safety-Expert Demonstration) on the other. The cells read Constrained RL, Cost-Constrained IL, Inverse Constrained RL and Dual-Expert IL. The last cell is bold and carries a red 'OUR SETTING' badge. The middle panel, Demonstrations, shows a grid maze with pink unsafe cells. Green safe-demonstration paths (D_S) wind around the unsafe cells, and orange performance paths (D_P) cut straight from the start s0 to the red goal flag. The right panel, Learned Policies, shows a green safe-region grid. A red 'Divergence' path detours along the safe data, while a blue 'Support' path goes directly to the goal. The eye goes first to the bold table cell, then to the colorful paths.
caption: { {(left)} Taxonomy of safe sequential decision-making problems by available performance and safety signals. {(middle)} Dual-expert IL instance: $\mathcal{D}_\rP$ prioritizes fast goal reaching but is possibly unsafe, while $\mathcal{D}_\rS$ stays safe but possibly suboptimal. {(right)} Prior offline IL relies on divergence regularization (e.g., behavior regularization), biasing the policy toward $\mathcal{D}_\rS$'s suboptimal behaviors (red path); DexDICE instead imposes a support constraint from $\mathcal{D}_\rS$ (blue path), recovering $\mathcal{D}_\rP$'s near-optimal route within the safe support. }
abstract: Ensuring high returns while providing strong safety guarantees in offline imitation learning (IL) is a fundamental challenge: existing approaches either rely on explicitly specified cost functions, which are difficult to design for complex real-world safety constraints, or require expert demonstrations that are both safe and high-performing, which are often too costly to collect. We introduce dual-expert imitation learning, which leverages two complementary data sources: (i) safety-compliant demonstrations that faithfully follow safety guidelines but may be suboptimal, and (ii) performance-oriented demonstrations that achieve high returns but may violate safety guidelines. To address this problem, we propose DexDICE (Dual-expert offline imitation learning via stationary DIstribution Correction Estimation). Instead of conventional distribution constraints, DexDICE combines DICE-style offline learning with safe support constraints, enabling agents to exploit high-return behaviors while remaining within safety-compliant regions. We prove that the ideal solution satisfying this constraint exactly has zero unsafe-region visitation with high probability. We evaluate DexDICE on a re-curated DSRL benchmark and validate it on a real-world mobile-robot navigation task trained directly from human teleoperation demonstrations, where it substantially outperforms baselines and remains robust to data scarcity and quality degradation.
